_meta.description: Harder tactical suite (v2) for the auto-research program, batch 2. The v1 suite (20 positions) did not discriminate: scoring v1, v2 and v3 all scored 20/20. These positions come from batch-1 lost games (prevention: the side to move missed the only prevention 1 ply before the decisive open four; setup: the winner's 2-ply setup 2 plies before it) plus hand-constructed VCF/VCT positions. Every expected-move list was verified exhaustively (ml/scripts/build_tactical_hard.py): prevention lists are exactly the moves that win, force a four, or leave the opponent with zero live open-four creators; setup lists are exactly the 2-ply setups; winning lists are exactly the 2-ply setups plus the VCF first moves; vcf positions pass iff the move starts a forced win by consecutive fours. v1's score on this suite is the clause-3 reference for batch-2 versions (see research/iterations/tactical-suite-v2.md). No batch-2 version was tuned on these positions.

positions.name: Create a double open three
positions.description: Hand-constructed control: Black has a horizontal two (5,7)-(6,7) and a vertical two (7,5)-(7,6). Only (7,7) completes both into open threes — White can block one, and Black extends the other into an open four. Every 1-ply engine finds this one (double-open-three bonus); it guards against regressions on easy setups.

positions.name: Quiet setup — open three plus double-four threat
positions.description: Hand-constructed: (7,7) looks quiet (one open three plus a closed three) but wins in two — it completes the horizontal open three and arms the double-four square (9,5), so White cannot stop both. (6,6) also wins (it creates a second open three). The tempting four-creating moves (9,4) and (9,5) score far higher in 1-ply: (9,5) does force a win by consecutive fours (so it passes too), but (9,4) does not — White blocks and the attack dies. Expected moves are exactly the verified winning moves (2-ply setups plus VCF first moves).

positions.name: Quiet setup — the 58k double three is a decoy
positions.description: Hand-constructed: the highest 1-ply moves here are double-open-three decoys — (9,7) scores 58,167 but its threats are gap-threes whose extensions give only single-ended fours, so White stops them. The winning moves are the quiet (7,7) (open three plus the armed double-four square (10,10)), (8,7) and (8,9) (2-ply setups), and (10,10) itself, which forces a win by consecutive fours. Expected moves are exactly the verified winning moves (2-ply setups plus VCF first moves).

positions.name: Race — take your open four instead of blocking
positions.description: Hand-constructed: Black holds an open-four creator (8,3) and a VCF sequence (9,6)/(10,6), but White holds an open three on row 11. The 1-ply engines block White's threat (8,11) — defence scores one point above the open four — and miss the forced win. Only a move starting a forced win by consecutive fours passes. The four-creating traps (8,7) and (8,2) do not force a win.

positions.name: Race (White to move) — take your open four
positions.description: Hand-constructed: the colour-swap of vcf-race-block-or-win — White holds the open-four creator (8,3) and the VCF sequence, Black holds the open three on row 11. Same trap: blocking scores above winning in 1-ply. Only a move starting a forced win by consecutive fours passes.

positions.name: Forced win — two-four sequence, quiet second four
positions.description: Hand-constructed: the forcing sequence needs two fours. (9,6) makes a four White must block at (10,6); only then does (10,7) make the open four on the diagonal (7,4)-(10,7) — (10,7) is not four-creating on move 1. The trap (10,6) also makes a four, but White's block at (9,6) occupies the square the sequence needs, so the attack dies. Only (9,6) starts a forced win.

positions.name: Forced win — two-four sequence, rotated
positions.description: Hand-constructed: vcf-two-four-sequence rotated 90 degrees. (6,5) makes a four White must block at (6,4); only then does (7,4) make the open four. The trap (6,4) also makes a four, but White's block at (6,5) occupies the square the sequence needs. Only (6,5) starts a forced win.
